Irene / team — short answers first, then details. Attaching an updated flow diagram and retention matrix.

Short answers:
- Soft-delete window (default): 30 days. During this window, objects are marked with a tombstone and excluded from normal reads but still present in replicas and snapshots.
- Expunge cadence (default): Background expunge job runs hourly per-region, but cross-region final removal (object-level expunge from archived snapshots) is executed in a rolling wave that finishes within 72 hours after the end of the soft-delete window. In other words, full hard delete = soft-delete_end + up to 72h under normal conditions.
- Legal-hold: legal-hold metadata is replicated inline with the object metadata and, when applied before expunge, prevents the background expunge job from removing the object from both local and remote snapshot repositories. Holds are honored automatically; opening a ticket is only required for emergency manual pinning or for air-gapped on-prem situations.
- Restore behavior: restores initiated within soft-delete keep incremental snapshot chains intact. We rebuild missing index shards lazily from adjacent snapshots; partial restores can show a short index rebuild delay (minutes to a few hours for large datasets). Full fidelity is preserved as long as the restore is performed before the final expunge.

Notes / tech detail:
- Replication model: we use asynchronous region-to-region replication for archived objects. Each region keeps an independent tombstone index. The expunge worker scans tombstones and associated snapshot manifests and then schedules object expunges. We batch object deletions to limit cross-region egress and avoid race conditions; this is why we have the 72h rolling window.
- Edge cases: if a replica region is temporarily unavailable, the expunge wave will skip that region and queue work for up to 14 days; after that we escalate and hold the expunge until either connectivity is restored or legal retention period expires.
- Evidence: attached flow diagram shows the message path and timing, and the retention matrix lists default values and enterprise-override options.

Attachments: backup-erasure-flow-v2.png, retention-policy-matrix.xlsx

Quick additions for the compliance note:

- Auditability: every tombstone and expunge action is recorded in the audit log (immutable events) with a correlation id that ties the original deletion request to subsequent expunge jobs across regions. We can provide an export with the correlation id mapping for GreenBank if they require evidence for an erasure cycle.
- SLA exceptions: enterprise customers can request reduced expunge windows (e.g., soft-delete_end + 24h) with a committed SLA; that requires reserved capacity to ensure the expunge wave completes within the tighter window.
- Support: for customers with strict legal holds we push a supplemental snapshot pin into a customer-controlled snapshot bucket (when Private or Dedicated). For hosted accounts, legal-hold metadata is sufficient and is managed by our control plane.
